newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up on late selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up on late selective buying.

text.p: Late overseas interest in a few big and medium-sized stocks combined with speculative buying in certain secondaries to help the Jakarta index end up on Tuesday after it experienced day-long downward pressure, brokers said.
The Composite Index rose 0.56 points, or 0.09 percent, to close at 656.65 points after touching an intra-day low of 654.08 points. Gainers led losers by 56 to 51, with 71 counters unchanged.
"Overall market sentiment was quite weak and in directionless trading today. I do not expect any big change tomorrow as the index will only moving in a narrow-range," a broker said.
Some brokers said they expected news from key overseas markets could boost buying in Jakarta on Wednesday, keeping the index in positive territory.

"Generally, there is no negative issues in the domestic market but it seems investors are taking a hold position. But I hope the higher closing today could inspire the market on Wednesday," a foreign broker said.

Heavyweight telecommunications firm Telkom and medium-sized stocks such as Kalbe Farma, Indah Kiat and Multipolar were among the active stocks which made handsome gains on overseas buying, brokers said.
Telkom closed at 4,200 rupiah on 1.3 million shares after falling 25 rupiah to 4,175 rupiah earlier.

Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma rose 300 rupiah to 3,400 rupiah on 3.6 million shares after hitting a high of 3,425 rupiah earlier which boosted by rumours of acquisitions and joint-venture, brokers said.
Kalbe Farma's corporate secretary Saka Abadi declined to comment on the market talk, adding there was nothing new to report about the company's activities.
"Investors are buying Kalbe Farma after other pharmaceutical stocks like Tempo Scan Pacific made significant gains recently," he told Reuters.
One analyst with a Japanese firm said Kalbe Farma's share rise was also linked to the belief that its prevailing price was quite cheap after it underperformed in 1996.
Paper maker Indah Kiat was actively traded after a report that it would benefit from either a steady or lower price of pulp due to sustained high levels of global pulp inventory, brokers said.
While Indah Kiat's price remained unchanged all day after opening at 1,725 rupiah, 1.2 million shares changed hands.
Secondary property firm Summarecon also made healthy gains on news that it planned to list one of its subsidiaries and launch two new projects this year, brokers said.
It rose 150 rupiah to 1,400 rupiah with about nine million shares changing hands after it was actively traded on talk that it might acquire another property firm.
Summarecon's corporate secretary Michael Yong, speaking to Reuters, denied the rumour.

Glass and ceramic maker Mulia Industri also made healthy gains on talk of a possible stock split. "I heard they will push up the price to 3,000 rupiah before announcing the plan to split it," a local broker said. Mulia Industri rose 75 rupiah to 2,700 rupiah.
